title: Backend-specific model selection and Codex catalogue refresh
status: Implementation design for the owner-authorized first model unit; no landing verdict
provenance: Tom, 5 September 2026 Melbourne: use supplied Astra export and start working through the Norn fixes
decisions: Keep the existing Sol default; import factual visible-model metadata on the Codex subscription route only. Preserve older model entries absent from this snapshot; absence is not retirement.
Astra alias is astra. Codex default and maximum windows remain distinct. No 300-400K hard planning cap is introduced.

Represent advertised ultra as an effort identifier, validate it against the actual selected backend/model, and document that this is not automatic task delegation. Live provider support is an explicit remaining verification, not inferred from fixtures.
Startup and live switching must use selected provider/backend and explicit context-override provenance; prepare/validate before mutating model, budgets and inherited context.
No changes to provider history, endpoint/auth selection, output-token policy or public API catalogue facts in this unit. These are separately tracked design work.

The current public Responses and compatible Chat catalogue entries are empty. Those routes require an explicit context window, and explicit effort/tier settings are refused as undeclared; no Codex capability is borrowed. This limitation must be visible in release notes until route-specific metadata is added.

A child may inherit its immediate parent’s operator-explicit context only when canonical model and concrete backend match. Explicit child policy wins. Derived windows and different model/route values are not inherited. Publish this provenance with live model selection and child contexts.
Bind the actual compaction reserve at prompt assembly. Refuse a live context-window transition that would enable or disable compaction while preserving the stable prompt and reserve.

problem: The supplied Codex catalogue has new model facts. Existing cross-backend lookups and partial switches can apply incorrect limits or capabilities, and child launches need explicit context provenance on uncatalogued routes.
